scenarios.scenario_context: An organization is implementing PRINCE2 7 as its standard project management methodology. The organization needs to understand the core principles, processes, and structure of PRINCE2 7 before launching its first project using this approach.

questions.stem: Which of the following best describes the core purpose of PRINCE2 7 as a project management methodology?

options.text: To provide a flexible, adaptable framework for managing projects effectively regardless of project type or size
options.justification: defines PRINCE2's universal applicability

options.text: To enforce a rigid, one-size-fits-all approach to all types of projects
options.justification: contradicts PRINCE2's tailoring principle

options.text: To replace all other project management approaches entirely
options.justification: not PRINCE2's intended scope

options.text: To manage only IT and software development projects
options.justification: PRINCE2 applies to all project types

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Introduction and Principles Overview
questions.explain_correct: PRINCE2 7 is designed as a tailorable, principles-based framework applicable to projects of all types and sizes.

explain_wrong.B: PRINCE2 emphasizes tailoring, not rigid application
explain_wrong.C: PRINCE2 complements rather than replaces other approaches
explain_wrong.D: PRINCE2 is universally applicable across all sectors and industries

questions.stem: What is the primary role of the Project Board in PRINCE2 7 governance?

options.text: To provide strategic direction, oversight, and authorization at the directing level of management
options.justification: defines board's governance responsibility

options.text: To execute all day-to-day project activities and deliver products
options.justification: that's the project manager's role

options.text: To perform all quality assurance and testing activities
options.justification: quality is distributed across roles

options.text: To manage supplier contracts independently without project oversight
options.justification: suppliers work under project governance

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 5 - Organization
questions.explain_correct: The Project Board is responsible for directing the project, providing strategic oversight, and making key authorization decisions.

explain_wrong.B: The Project Manager executes day-to-day activities under board direction
explain_wrong.C: Quality is managed through the Quality practice, not exclusively by the board
explain_wrong.D: Suppliers are integrated into the project's governance structure

questions.stem: At what stage of the project should the Business Case be established and maintained?

options.text: Only at project initiation, then it should not be changed
options.justification: contradicts continued justification principle

options.text: Throughout the project lifecycle to ensure continued business justification at every stage boundary
options.justification: reflects continued justification principle

options.text: Only during project closure when evaluating outcomes
options.justification: too late; decisions made earlier

options.text: Only when the Project Board specifically requests it
options.justification: should be routine, not ad-hoc

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 2 - Continued Business Justification
questions.explain_correct: The Business Case must be maintained throughout the project and reviewed at every stage boundary to ensure the project remains viable and aligned with business objectives.

explain_wrong.A: The Business Case must evolve as circumstances change
explain_wrong.C: Evaluation at closure is too late to influence project decisions
explain_wrong.D: Business Case maintenance is a continuous responsibility, not ad-hoc

scenarios.scenario_context: An organization is learning about the seven PRINCE2 processes and how they structure project delivery. Understanding these processes is essential before tailoring PRINCE2 for specific project contexts.

questions.stem: Which process establishes the initial approach and authorization to proceed with project initiation?

options.text: Starting Up a Project
options.justification: is the first process in PRINCE2

options.text: Initiating a Project
options.justification: comes after Starting Up

options.text: Controlling a Stage
options.justification: is an execution process

options.text: Closing a Project
options.justification: is the final process

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 17 - Starting Up a Project
questions.explain_correct: Starting Up a Project is the first process, executed before formal project initiation, to establish the fundamental project approach and secure authorization to proceed.

explain_wrong.B: Initiating a Project is the second process
explain_wrong.C: Controlling a Stage manages ongoing stage execution
explain_wrong.D: Closing a Project is the final process

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of the Initiating a Project process?

options.text: To establish the detailed project plans, business case, and authorization for the first stage
options.justification: defines purpose of initiation

options.text: To execute and deliver project products according to the stage plan
options.justification: that's the controlling process

options.text: To monitor project progress and manage issues and changes
options.justification: also part of controlling

options.text: To create a quick startup document without detailed planning
options.justification: initiation requires comprehensive planning

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 18 - Initiating a Project
questions.explain_correct: Initiating a Project creates the detailed project plans, confirms the business justification, and establishes the foundation for project execution.

explain_wrong.B: Execution and product delivery occur during Controlling a Stage
explain_wrong.C: Monitoring and change management occur throughout Controlling a Stage
explain_wrong.D: Initiation requires comprehensive planning and documentation

questions.stem: What is the main focus of the Controlling a Stage process?

options.text: To manage the day-to-day execution of stage work, monitoring progress, and handling issues and changes
options.justification: defines controlling purpose

options.text: To approve the final closure of the entire project
options.justification: that's closing

options.text: To establish the high-level project approach and business case
options.justification: that's initiation

options.text: To move to the next stage without reviewing current stage performance
options.justification: stage boundaries require reviews

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 20 - Controlling a Stage
questions.explain_correct: Controlling a Stage is the core execution process that manages the delivery of stage work, monitors progress against tolerances, and handles issues and changes.

explain_wrong.B: Closing a Project handles project closure, not Controlling a Stage
explain_wrong.C: Initiating a Project establishes the business case and approach
explain_wrong.D: Stage boundaries require formal assessment of stage completion

scenarios.scenario_context: A project team is learning about PRINCE2 practices, including plans, quality, change control, and risk management. These practices provide the day-to-day techniques and tools for managing projects.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Project Plan in PRINCE2?

options.text: To provide a high-level baseline for project delivery that defines how the project objectives will be achieved
options.justification: defines project plan purpose

options.text: To record daily team activities and minor decisions
options.justification: that's the daily log

options.text: To replace the need for stage plans entirely
options.justification: project and stage plans serve different purposes

options.text: To manage supplier contract payments
options.justification: plans don't manage contracts

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 7 - Plans Practice
questions.explain_correct: The Project Plan is a high-level, board-level document that outlines how the project will achieve its objectives and shows the overall project strategy.

explain_wrong.B: Daily activities are recorded in logs, not the project plan
explain_wrong.C: Stage plans are required in addition to the project plan
explain_wrong.D: Contract management is separate from planning

questions.stem: What does the Quality practice define in PRINCE2?

options.text: The standards that products must meet and how quality will be assured throughout the project
options.justification: defines quality practice scope

options.text: Only the final acceptance testing at project closure
options.justification: quality is continuous, not final

options.text: The budget available for quality-related activities
options.justification: quality is about standards, not budget

options.text: The project manager's personal quality expectations
options.justification: quality is objective and documented

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 7 - Quality Practice
questions.explain_correct: The Quality practice establishes quality standards for all products and defines how quality assurance and quality control will be applied throughout the project.

explain_wrong.B: Quality assurance and control occurs throughout the project, not just at closure
explain_wrong.C: Quality is about standards and acceptance criteria, not budget allocation
explain_wrong.D: Quality standards must be objective, documented, and agreed by stakeholders

questions.stem: What is the primary objective of the Risk practice in PRINCE2?

options.text: To identify, assess, and manage risks and uncertainties that could affect project success
options.justification: defines risk practice purpose

options.text: To eliminate all risks from the project completely
options.justification: some risks are unavoidable

options.text: To assign blame when things go wrong
options.justification: risk is about prevention and management

options.text: To increase project budget to cover any possible problems
options.justification: risk management is not just about budget

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 7 - Risk Practice
questions.explain_correct: The Risk practice enables the project to identify, analyze, and respond to risks proactively throughout the project lifecycle.

explain_wrong.B: Risk elimination is impossible; risk management focuses on mitigation and control
explain_wrong.C: Risk management is preventive and collaborative, not about assigning blame
explain_wrong.D: Risk management includes various response strategies beyond budget allocation

scenarios.scenario_context: An organization is establishing the key PRINCE2 roles and defining the organizational structure for project governance. Understanding the roles and their responsibilities is critical for effective project management.

questions.stem: Who is responsible for maintaining the Business Case throughout the project?

options.text: The Executive, who owns the investment and business justification
options.justification: executive owns business case

options.text: The Project Manager, who is responsible for all project administration
options.justification: manager controls execution, not business case ownership

options.text: The Senior User, who represents the project benefits
options.justification: user represents benefits but not business case owner

options.text: The Project Board collectively without specific role assignment
options.justification: executive has specific accountability

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 5 - Organization
questions.explain_correct: The Executive is the project sponsor and is accountable for the business case, ensuring ongoing business justification throughout the project.

explain_wrong.B: The Project Manager manages day-to-day execution under executive direction
explain_wrong.C: The Senior User focuses on requirements and benefits realization
explain_wrong.D: While the board oversees it, the Executive has specific accountability for the business case

questions.stem: What is the primary responsibility of the Senior User role?

options.text: To represent user interests, define requirements, and ensure benefits are delivered
options.justification: defines senior user role

options.text: To manage all project finances and expenditure
options.justification: that's typically an executive function

options.text: To execute all technical product delivery
options.justification: that's the supplier's role

options.text: To approve all project manager decisions without question
options.justification: the board collectively makes approvals

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 5 - Organization
questions.explain_correct: The Senior User represents the interests of those who will use the project's products and ensures that user needs and benefits requirements are met.

explain_wrong.B: Financial management is the Executive's responsibility
explain_wrong.C: Product delivery is the responsibility of the Senior Supplier/suppliers
explain_wrong.D: The board makes decisions collectively based on recommendations

questions.stem: What is the role of the Senior Supplier in PRINCE2?

options.text: To represent supplier interests and ensure that delivery resources and expertise are available
options.justification: defines senior supplier role

options.text: To manage day-to-day project execution and issue control
options.justification: that's the project manager

options.text: To define all user requirements for the project
options.justification: that's the senior user

options.text: To provide financing for the project
options.justification: that's the executive's responsibility

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 5 - Organization
questions.explain_correct: The Senior Supplier represents the interests of those who will provide the project's products and ensures adequate resources, expertise, and technical capability.

explain_wrong.B: The Project Manager handles day-to-day execution
explain_wrong.C: The Senior User defines requirements
explain_wrong.D: The Executive provides the business justification and budget approval

scenarios.scenario_context: A project team needs to understand the essential PRINCE2 management products and documents that form the foundation of project governance and control. These products enable effective communication and decision-making.

questions.stem: Which document defines the overall approach for how a project will be managed and governed?

options.text: Project Management Approach
options.justification: Correct - defines how project will be managed

options.text: Stage Plan, which contains detailed activities for the current stage only
options.justification: Incorrect - Stage Plan is for current stage, not overall approach

options.text: Project Brief, which outlines high-level requirements
options.justification: Incorrect - Project Brief outlines requirements, not management approach

options.text: Quality Register, which tracks quality metrics and issues
options.justification: Incorrect - Quality Register tracks quality items, not management approach

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 4 - Tailoring
questions.explain_correct: The Project Management Approach describes how PRINCE2 will be tailored and applied to the specific project, defining governance and management strategies.

explain_wrong.B: Stage Plans detail execution within a specific stage
explain_wrong.C: The Daily Log is used for recording day-to-day issues and decisions
explain_wrong.D: Quality Register tracks quality-related activities and metrics

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a Product Description in PRINCE2?

options.text: To define the quality criteria and acceptance standards for a specific product
options.justification: defines product description purpose

options.text: To record all changes requested to a product
options.justification: that's change control

options.text: To list all suppliers involved in delivery
options.justification: that's supplier management

options.text: To estimate the cost of producing a product
options.justification: that's estimating

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 7 - Quality Practice
questions.explain_correct: A Product Description defines what a product is, its quality criteria, acceptance standards, and customer expectations.

explain_wrong.B: Change requests are managed through the Issue and Change practice
explain_wrong.C: Supplier involvement is managed separately through the organization
explain_wrong.D: Cost estimation is part of the planning process

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of monitoring progress in PRINCE2?

options.text: To track actual progress against the plan and take corrective action if tolerances are exceeded
options.justification: defines progress monitoring purpose

options.text: To record detailed timesheets for all team members
options.justification: that's HR administration

options.text: To blame team members when delays occur
options.justification: monitoring is for control, not blame

options.text: To eliminate the need for any schedule changes
options.justification: changes are managed, not eliminated

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 11 - Progress Practice
questions.explain_correct: Progress monitoring compares actual project performance against planned targets and enables timely corrective action to keep the project on track.

explain_wrong.B: Timesheets are HR administration, separate from progress monitoring
explain_wrong.C: Monitoring is for control and corrective action, not blame assignment
explain_wrong.D: Change management is an essential part of project control

scenarios.scenario_context: A project team is learning how PRINCE2 is tailored to fit different project contexts and how stage boundaries provide control points for decision-making and governance.

questions.stem: What does tailoring PRINCE2 mean?

options.text: Adapting PRINCE2 principles, processes, and practices to fit the specific context and needs of the project
options.justification: defines tailoring purpose

options.text: Ignoring PRINCE2 framework elements that don't seem relevant
options.justification: tailoring is intentional, not ad-hoc

options.text: Applying PRINCE2 exactly as written in all situations
options.justification: that contradicts the need for tailoring

options.text: Using only the processes without the principles and practices
options.justification: tailoring applies to all elements

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 4 - Tailoring
questions.explain_correct: Tailoring is the process of adapting PRINCE2 to suit the specific environment, culture, and requirements of the project while maintaining the core principles.

explain_wrong.B: Tailoring is deliberate and documented, not ad-hoc omission
explain_wrong.C: PRINCE2 is inherently designed to be tailored to different contexts
explain_wrong.D: All elements of PRINCE2 (principles, processes, practices) may be tailored

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of a stage boundary in PRINCE2?

options.text: To provide a formal control point where the Project Board reviews progress and authorizes the next stage
options.justification: defines stage boundary purpose

options.text: To allow the project manager to take a vacation between stages
options.justification: not the purpose of stage boundaries

options.text: To mark the point where team members are reassigned to other projects
options.justification: that may happen, but it's not the purpose

options.text: To automatically approve all requested project changes
options.justification: changes must be assessed

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 21 - Managing a Stage Boundary
questions.explain_correct: Stage boundaries are formal management control points where the Project Board reviews stage performance and decides whether to authorize the next stage.

explain_wrong.B: Stage boundaries are control mechanisms, not scheduling breaks
explain_wrong.C: While resource changes may occur, that's not the formal purpose
explain_wrong.D: Changes are assessed and managed; stage boundaries don't automatically approve anything

questions.stem: Why is business justification reviewed at every stage boundary in PRINCE2?

options.text: To ensure the project remains aligned with business objectives and that continued investment is justified
options.justification: defines continued justification principle

options.text: To punish the project team if they fall behind schedule
options.justification: justification is about business viability

options.text: To ensure no changes are ever made to the project
options.justification: reviews enable managed change

options.text: To eliminate the project manager's role and decision-making authority
options.justification: reviews support governance, not eliminate roles

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 2 - Continued Business Justification Principle
questions.explain_correct: The principle of continued business justification requires that a project remains viable and aligned with business benefits throughout its lifecycle, reviewed at key decision points.

explain_wrong.B: Business case review is about business viability, not performance punishment
explain_wrong.C: Regular justification review enables controlled change, not prevents it
explain_wrong.D: Governance mechanisms support effective management, they don't eliminate roles

scenarios.scenario_context: BioPharma is executing Stage 3 (Clinical Trials & Regulatory Compliance) for a volatile therapeutic drug asset under strict corporate expenditure limits. The risk environment fluctuates daily due to changing international healthcare legislation. The Senior Supplier (Director of Laboratory Research) must ensure all laboratory checks strictly match international molecular benchmarks.

questions.stem: The project is at a stage boundary. The Vice President of Medical Affairs (Senior User) notes that changing healthcare legislation will increase the administrative cost of tracking clinical trials by £40,000, though the drug’s projected market value remains highly profitable. What is the correct next step for the project framework?

options.text: The project manager should immediately log the cost increase in the Daily Log and monitor for trends
options.justification: Incorrect - PM logs it but must escalate to Executive for approval

options.text: The Executive must update the Business Case with the new cost and submit to Project Board for decision
options.justification: Correct - Business Case must be updated at stage boundaries

options.text: The Team Manager should adjust the Stage Plan baseline to accommodate the increase without further escalation
options.justification: Incorrect - Stage Plan adjustments require executive approval if exceeding tolerance

options.text: Project Assurance should verify the financial variance and confirm it falls within approved baseline tolerance
options.justification: Incorrect - If outside tolerance, must escalate, not just verify

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 2 (Principles - Ensure Continued Business Justification) & Chapter 6 (Business Case Practice)
questions.explain_correct: The Executive owns the Business Case and must re-verify that the project remains a worthwhile investment whenever factors alter the financial parameters, explicitly executed at stage boundaries.

explain_wrong.A: The project manager cannot bypass the board or unilaterally allocate funds for a baseline change via the daily log.
explain_wrong.C: Accountability for business justification rests with the Executive, not the Senior Supplier or delivery layer.
explain_wrong.D: Cost variations do not cause automatic termination if the project remains net-positive, desirable, and strategically aligned.

questions.stem: The Director of Laboratory Research argues that because their internal chemical stability checking methodologies are highly proprietary, they should not record individual test failures within the project's centralized Quality Register. Is this position valid?

options.text: Yes, because proprietary supplier workflows are entirely insulated from customer management tracking products
options.justification: ensuring commercial vendors protect intellectual property assets during active testing sweeps.

options.text: No, because the Quality Register must record all planned and executed quality activities across the project to maintain control
options.justification: providing the project manager with the necessary progress data to monitor quality performance variables and verify that deliverables are fit for purpose before work package closure.

options.text: Yes, because the project manager only requires visibility into quality test logs during the final closing a project process
options.justification: negating the need for active tracking during intermediate execution stages.

options.text: No, because only the Senior User possesses the individual contractual authority to write quality status updates directly into the supplier's registers
options.justification: blocking the project manager from accessing raw laboratory validation sheets.

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 7 (Quality Practice - Quality Register) & Chapter 15 (Controlling a Stage Process)
questions.explain_correct: The Quality Register is a mandatory management product. It must maintain a complete, centralized record of all quality controls, tests, and reviews to enable effective progress tracking and control by the project manager.

explain_wrong.A: Proprietary workflows do not absolve a project from logging standard quality controls required to guarantee governance and safety compliance.
explain_wrong.C: Waiting until closure to view quality data introduces catastrophic risk; quality must be tracked dynamically within stages.
explain_wrong.D: The project manager maintains and reviews the Quality Register as part of stage control, not the Senior User.

scenarios.scenario_context: The Urban Core Transit project operates inside a high-maturity organizational context delivered as part of a regional rail infrastructure portfolio framework. Strained relationships exist between the municipal government representatives (the Customer) and the civil engineering consortium (the Supplier) regarding cost overrun liabilities and sustainability reporting frequencies.

questions.stem: The civil engineering consortium manager wants to know the exact frequency and day of the week they must submit their localized construction progress summaries to the project manager during Stage 4. Which product contains this information?

options.text: The Communication Management Approach
options.justification: because it defines the formal rules, reporting types, frequencies, and responsibilities for all information exchange between project stakeholders and management layers, supporting relationship alignment under the People element.

options.text: The Configuration Item Record metadata sheets
options.justification: because configuration management trackers link team progress updates directly to the physical structural properties of concrete pillars.

options.text: The Project Product Description text layout
options.justification: because customer quality expectations dictate the weekly progress meeting schedules for external supplier networks.

options.text: The long-term Benefits Management Approach blueprint
options.justification: because tactical engineering checkpoint intervals must match the 10-year macroeconomic tax credit audit timeline.

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 3 (People Element) & Appendix A (Communication Management Approach)
questions.explain_correct: The Communication Management Approach is the definitive source for establishing the timing, formats, and channels for progress reporting across all project management layers.

explain_wrong.B: Configuration records track version history and asset relationships, not team reporting calendars.
explain_wrong.C: The Project Product Description establishes output requirements, not operational management reporting cadences.
explain_wrong.D: The Benefits Management Approach maps post-project outcome measurements, not active stage progress reporting frequencies.

questions.stem: Strained relationships between the customer and supplier engineers regarding scope interpretations are delaying layout choices. The project manager wants to apply a structured set of training and alignment workshops to guide the teams through the new collaboration framework. Where should these actions be formalized?

options.text: Inside the Risk Register as a mitigation transfer response strategy
options.justification: ensuring commercial liability for team relationships is offloaded to a third-party legal mediator.

options.text: Within the Change Management Approach
options.justification: because the change management approach defines the specific interventions, training plans, and stakeholder activities required to manage human and behavioral transformations, directly supporting collaboration under the People element.

options.text: Directly within the baseline Project Product Description text layout
options.justification: to alter the final customer quality acceptance parameters to match supplier behavioral performance metrics.

options.text: In the informal Daily Log as an unmanaged personal journal reminder
options.justification: to keep relational tracking data completely confidential from the project board steering committee.

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 3 (People Element) & Appendix A (Change Management Approach)
questions.explain_correct: The change management approach outlines the specific interventions needed to facilitate organizational and human shifts, ensuring project roles collaborate effectively to adopt new processes.

explain_wrong.A: Team relationship workshops are behavioral change interventions, not legal risk transfer mechanisms.
explain_wrong.C: The Project Product Description governs product deliverables, not team interaction and cultural alignment methods.
explain_wrong.D: Structured alignment interventions impacting project performance targets must be formally planned in an approach document, not hidden in a scratchpad.

scenarios.scenario_context: GlobalRetail is executing a major overhaul of its consumer mobile shopping application. The project relies on a hybrid delivery model: the user-facing storefront utilizes an iterative-incremental (Agile) approach across 2-week sprints, while the underlying payment integration and secure server warehouse infrastructure follow a linear-sequential path. The project is currently in Stage 3 (Payment Gateway & Interface Integration). Corporate sustainability performance targets require minimizing data-center server carbon emissions by 15% through optimized code execution parameters.

questions.stem: An agile development team raises a change request to introduce an instant-checkout feature on the storefront application. The impact assessment reveals that implementing this feature will require an additional £8,000 from the designated change budget but will not threaten stage-level cost or time tolerances. The project board has previously delegated change authority to a specific Change Advisory Group for storefront modifications up to £10,000. Which action is correct?

options.text: The project manager must halt the active sprint and submit an Exception Report to the Executive
options.justification: because any alteration to the approved storefront functional scope baseline must be evaluated by the directing level to maintain commercial alignment.

options.text: The Change Advisory Group possesses the authority to review and approve the change request directly
options.justification: because under the PRINCE2 7 Issue Practice, the project board can delegate change authority to a specific individual or group to manage modifications within an explicit budget limit, optimizing decision velocity.

options.text: The agile development team can implement the instant-checkout button immediately without formal logging
options.justification: because iterative delivery frameworks grant absolute scope autonomy to the delivery layer during an active time-box.

options.text: Log the modification request exclusively inside the long-term Benefits Management Approach ledger
options.justification: because any user interface adjustments instantly change the financial return-on-investment parameters of the corporate retail portal.

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 10 (Issue Practice - Change Authority and Budgets) & Chapter 15 (Controlling a Stage Process)
questions.explain_correct: The project board can delegate change authority to a separate body to handle changes within defined financial limits. Since the change budget impact (£8,000) falls below the delegated threshold (£10,000) and stays within stage tolerances, the Change Advisory Group can authorize it.

explain_wrong.A: An Exception Report is only triggered if a stage or project-level tolerance boundary is forecast to be breached, which is not the case here.
explain_wrong.C: Agile teams must operate within the constraints of their authorized work packages; they cannot change product baselines without formal change control handling.
explain_wrong.D: The Benefits Management Approach plans the measurement of post-project outcomes; it does not track or authorize active technical code modifications within a stage.

questions.stem: The project manager needs to determine if the development of the payment gateway interface is deviating from the authorized plan. The agile delivery team records their daily progress using burn-up charts and automated Kanban boards. How should the project manager handle this progress tracking data?

options.text: Reject the agile team's tracking metrics and force them to populate manual Gantt charts daily
options.justification: because PRINCE2 7 requires all execution progress to be documented using linear-sequential scheduling tools exclusively.

options.text: Utilize the team's automated charts and velocity statistics to inform work package monitoring and populate formal reports
options.justification: because the progress practice supports using delivery-level tools and agile metrics to assess execution speed, adapting the governance context to match the delivery method without creating unnecessary duplication.

options.text: Instruct the Senior Supplier to verify every daily code change personally before updating the stage log
options.justification: because the directing layer must maintain continuous hands-on command over the physical delivery tasks within a sprint.

options.text: Omit weekly progress evaluations and rely entirely on the final project closure review
options.justification: since hybrid e-commerce projects are exempt from tracking intermediate stage deviations under corporate governance frameworks.

questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 4 (Delivery Methods), Chapter 11 (Progress Practice), & Chapter 16 (Managing Product Delivery Process)
questions.explain_correct: PRINCE2 7 explicitly embraces agile delivery methods. The project manager can leverage delivery-level progress metrics (like velocity or Kanban charts) to monitor work package performance and generate highlight reports, matching the delivery context.

explain_wrong.A: PRINCE2 7 does not restrict progress tracking to linear tools like Gantt charts; it allows tailoring to integrate with agile frameworks.
explain_wrong.C: The Senior Supplier provides strategic governance and assurance; forcing them to micromanage daily code commits violates role separation principles.
explain_wrong.D: Relying solely on project closure breaks active control protocols and exposes the stage baseline to unmanaged tolerance breaches.

explain_wrong.A: Detailed planning of individual tasks 18 months in advance results in inaccurate plans that collapse when the first baseline variation occurs.
explain_wrong.C: PRINCE2 7 explicitly structures control stage-by-stage and supports rolling-wave planning methods; forcing all future stages to be detailed at once is incorrect.
explain_wrong.D: The project manager is responsible for creating and maintaining project and stage plans, aligned with the board's directed boundaries, not the Team Manager.

questions.stem: The CCB receives a change request to update the data formatting logic to comply with an incoming banking regulation. questions.citation: PRINCE2 7 Manual, Chapter 10 (Issue Practice - Change Authority Delegations) & Chapter 14 (Directing a Project Process)
questions.explain_correct: A Change Authority operates under explicit boundaries delegated by the Project Board. The Change Authority cannot approve it and must refer the matter to the Project Board, who hold ultimate directing accountability.

explain_wrong.A: A Change Authority’s power is bounded; they cannot unilaterally approve changes that break overall stage tolerances or impact project justification.
explain_wrong.C: Using personal funds to hide corporate project overruns breaks standard financial governance, compromises data tracking, and violates professional ethics.
